findings.title: Keep optional-case fragment targets on the disclosure
findings.evidence: renderSection retains id=planning-2, planning-3, planning-4, planning-5 and related-cases on an outer section, then places the previously visible body in a closed child details. The generated table of contents still links to those ids. src/assets/site-navigation.js:6 only opens target.closest(details) and ancestor disclosures, so these links do not reveal their case content.
findings.reproduction: Open /guides/timed-booking-handoff/#planning-2 or select that entry in In this guide. The page scrolls to a closed summary and the referenced case stays hidden.
findings.impact: Existing deep links and the guide contents no longer reveal the requested case; visitors must discover and open it manually.
findings.minimalFix: For optional cases, put the existing id on details and omit it from the wrapper section. Alternatively, make the shared reveal handler open this specific direct child disclosure.
findings.verification: Static markup and shared anchor-handler inspection; a minimal VM invocation of the existing handler with an outer-section target confirms no disclosure-open path.
findings.resolution: Primary moved the existing optional-case fragment id onto details and removed it from the wrapper. Source fix verified; primary will verify direct links, table-of-contents links and history navigation in browser.

remainingAuditItems.item: Queens multilingual FAQ remains firing-specific. The local worker ledger explicitly deferred broadening it because FAQs were outside that worker ownership.
remainingAuditItems.minimalFix: Broaden the question and answer to translation of the buyer business service/preparation/inquiry pages, retaining owner approval, maintenance and reply-language boundaries.
